title: Concerto
identity: Torke’s Saxophone Concerto is for soprano saxophone and orchestra, composed in 1993, about 18 minutes, premiered by John Harle with the Albany Symphony on 14 January 1994. The composer’s note describes flowing sixteenth-note decorations in movement I and records the premiere-day recording.

evidence.claim: Opened composer page gives instrumentation, 1993 date, 18-minute duration, premiere and recording history, and composer explanation of movement I’s flowing sixteenth notes.
Composer page says the concerto has been recorded twice and played often; no audio was auditioned.

review_focus: Inference from the composer’s note: the flowing sixteenth-note decorations in movement I invite review of breath planning and coordination with the orchestral texture; this is a question for score study, not a claim about the complete solo part.
collection_flag: Original commissioned soprano saxophone concerto with orchestral and piano-reduction versions.

listening.description: Composer says the work was recorded twice and links the release Three.
listening.verification: Composer page checked; recording not auditioned.

score_links.description: Composer page with work note and score/publisher links; no notation preview inspected.

gaps: No saxophone notation was available to inspect; complete written range, articulation detail, and note-level demands remain unknown.
